basis: Skeletal dysplasia, sensorineural hearing loss and cleft palate define the syndrome; ocular abnormalities are explicitly absent.
Lymphatic vascular/perivascular neoplasm; pulmonary involvement depends on tumour location and is not established in most patients.
Inherited melanin biosynthesis disorder defining skin/hair hypopigmentation and ocular developmental abnormalities with impaired vision.
Iron metabolism disorder; hepatic injury supported by elevated transaminases in 5/7. Skin pigmentation alone lacks functional damage; cardiac and joint damage are minority findings.
Defined by structurally enlarged, tortuous veins; anatomical subtypes do not establish damage to additional organs across the group.
Melanocytic malignancy originating in acral skin, including palms, soles and nail units.
Congenital absence or hypoplasia of the iris; extraocular manifestations belong to particular syndromic subtypes.
Necrosis directly affects mandibular or maxillary bone; oral location alone does not establish additional mucosal disease.
Chronic bacterial infection of cervicofacial subcutaneous tissues with infiltrative abscesses and sinus tracts; jaw osteomyelitis is not universal.
Airway ciliary dysfunction defines disease. Chronic middle-ear disease is common in PCD (>50%); recurrent otitis is reported in 1/1 annotated patient.
Tumour originates in the retina; associated von Hippel-Lindau disease does not establish systemic involvement by this retinal tumour.
Severe neurodevelopmental disease with epilepsy and defining cataracts (5/7); feeding difficulties and central hypotonia do not establish gut or muscle disease.
Complex congenital heart malformations define the phenotype; abdominal situs inversus alone does not indicate abdominal organ dysfunction.
Cortical malformation with microcephaly and developmental impairment; optic atrophy occurs in 1/5, below threshold. Facial dysmorphism adds no damaged organ.
Myoclonus, cerebellar ataxia and sensorineural hearing loss define the syndrome; amyotrophy accompanies neuropathy rather than establishing primary muscle disease.
Metabolic myopathy, acidosis and deafness define disease; seizures, dystonia and spasticity support neurologic involvement in 1/1 annotated patient; evidence is sparse.
Immune-mediated rheumatic inflammation directly affects the pericardium.
Macrothrombocytopenia and progressive sensorineural hearing loss define the syndrome; enamel abnormalities are occasional.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with severe intellectual disability, motor and speech delay, seizures and central motor abnormalities; no independent muscle disease established.
External and middle-ear malformations cause conductive deafness; micrognathia alone does not establish additional functional skeletal disease.
Connective/soft-tissue stromal neoplasm; vascular proliferation is a tumour feature and does not establish separate cardiovascular damage.
Ivermectin poisoning characteristically causes CNS toxicity, including ataxia, altered consciousness and seizures; transient gastrointestinal symptoms add no organ.
Hereditary chorea with defining nystagmus and cataracts establishes neurologic and ocular disease.
Usually immune-mediated inflammation of the pars plana and adjacent vitreous; macular injury remains ocular. Extraocular disease is uncommon or separately diagnosed.
Inherited globin synthesis disorder causing microcytic anemia; no common direct extrahematologic damage established.
